evidence: src/domain/services/StockManager.ts: class StockManager has exactly three methods, canReserveStock, reserveStock and releaseStock, all about order stock reservation.
canReserveStock calls product.canReserve(line.quantity), so the reservation rule stays on Product and is not copied here.
reserveStock calls product.reserve(line.quantity) and releaseStock calls product.release(line.quantity), so stock changes go through the entity's own methods.
products.find(p => p.id === line.productId) is repeated in all three methods. This is a repeated lookup, not a duplicated business rule.
Only outgoing dependencies: src/domain/entities/Order.ts and src/domain/entities/Product.ts, both inside the domain module.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has one file, src/domain/services/StockManager.ts, and it handles a single concern: reserving and releasing product stock for the lines of an order. All three methods leave the stock rules to the Product entity, calling canReserve, reserve and release. The service never reads or changes stock quantities directly, so it does not bypass the domain's own abstractions, and each stock rule lives in one place. Each method repeats the same lookup, products.find(p => p.id === line.productId). This is a small refactoring opportunity, not a duplicated business rule. One inconsistency is worth noting but does not break the rule: canReserveStock returns false when a product is missing, while reserveStock and releaseStock skip a missing product without reporting it. The file stays cohesive and within its boundary.
